intent.text: rec: From the identity vantage, the prefix has to run without a prompt. If it needs approval, agents either stall or lose attribution, and vsect and the git trailers then cannot tell who acted. So removing the rule outright breaks the record. I recommend keep, with three conditions. (1) Scope: ses is right that a rule in the global ~/.claude/settings.json reaches every session on this machine. Narrow it to the agent-run environment, or to project settings, if the harness allows that. (2) Verify before relying on it: how the two PreToolUse hooks combine when both rewrite Bash, and whether the rewritten command still parses as a bare export after the second hook runs. (3) Check the failure mode. If the export is ever refused, the agent should fail loudly rather than run the command unattributed. A silent fallback would corrupt the record. I would not call the README's safety argument verified until those three points are tested.
